([[Glendale, Arizona]]) | college = [[Yakima Valley College|Yakima Valley]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–present | team1 = [[NBA G League Ignite]] | highlights = }} '''MarJon Beauchamp''' (born October 12, 2000; pronounced {{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|ɑːr|ʒ|ɒ|n|nbsp|ˈ|b|oʊ|tʃ|æ|m|p}}{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KRJREoNsAD0|title=Baseline Basics: MarJon Beauchamp|publisher=[[NBA G League]]|date=2021-10-25|accessdate=2022-02-11|time=0:08}}) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Yakima Valley College]]'s Yaks. ==High school career== Entering high school, Beauchamp moved from his hometown of [[Yakima, Washington]], to [[Seattle]] to play basketball at [[Nathan Hale High School (Washington)|Nathan Hale High School]] under head coach [[Brandon Roy]] and to face stronger competition.{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=With addition of five-star guard MarJon Beauchamp, Rainier Beach could be the state favorite again |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/with-addition-of-five-star-marjon-beauchamp-rainier-beach-a-state-contender-again/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=November 26, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Saez |first1=Rosin |title=Meet Washington’s Most Promising Basketball Star |url=https://www.seattlemet.com/articles/2019/2/19/meet-washington-s-most-promising-basketball-star |website=[[Seattle Metropolitan]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=February 19, 2019}} As a freshman, he was a deep reserve for a team that featured top recruits [[Michael Porter Jr.]] and [[Jontay Porter]].{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=Rainier Beach five-star recruit MarJon Beauchamp is transferring to Arizona prep school |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/rainier-beachs-marjon-beauchamp-is-transferring-to-arizona-prep-school/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=June 7, 2019}} Nathan Hale finished with a 29–0 record, won the [[Washington Interscholastic Activities Association]] Class 3A state title, and captured the No. 1 national ranking from [[MaxPreps]].{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=Nathan Hale finishes off perfect season with a flourish, beating Garfield for Class 3A state title |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/nathan-hale-finishes-off-perfect-season-with-a-flourish-beating-garfield-for-class-3a-state-title/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=March 4, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Hickman |first1=Jason |title=Final 2016-17 MaxPreps High School Top 25 Boys Basketball Rankings |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/m6mNCn3U0Uq6fWdm19xzRg/final-2016-17-maxpreps-high-school-top-25-boys-basketball-rankings-.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=March 31, 2017}} As a sophomore, Beauchamp transferred to [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]] in Seattle.{{cite web |last1=Prezkop |first1=Dylan |title=Player Intro: 2020 Wing MarJon Beauchamp |url=https://www.nextuprecruits.com/news_article/show/800215 |publisher=Next Up Recruits |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=June 26, 2017}} He moved to the school with former Nathan Hale coach Brandon Roy and teammate P. J. Fuller.{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=Boys basketball preview: Addition of P.J. Fuller makes loaded Garfield even more dangerous |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball-preview-addition-of-p-j-fuller-makes-loaded-garfield-even-more-dangerous/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=December 7, 2017}} He won his second straight Class 4A state championship and helped Garfield reach the quarterfinals at High School Nationals.{{cite web |title=No. 2 Oak Hill Academy dominates No. 12 Garfield in GEICO Nationals quarterfinals |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mH_dU1n6WEmV2zyu0ennlw/no-2-oak-hill-academy-dominates-no-12-garfield-in-geico-nationals-quarterfinals.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=March 29, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Lommers |first1=Aaron |title=Tacoma native Pierre Crockrell Jr. has breakout tournament, leads Garfield to 3A state championship |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article203413539.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=March 4, 2018}} For his junior season, Beauchamp transferred to [[Rainier Beach High School]] in Seattle, citing a lack of motivation in class and sickness from [[Mold (fungus)|mold]] in his house during his time at Garfield. He moved to the [[South End, Seattle|South End]], within school boundaries, and as a result was ruled eligible to play basketball for his new school. After leading Rainier Beach to league and district titles, he was named [[most valuable player]] of the Seattle 3A [[Metro League (Seattle)|Metro League]].{{cite web |title=Rainier Beach’s Marjon Beauchamp named 2019 Metro League boys basketball MVP (Seattle All-Metro teams) |url=https://sblivewa.com/2019/02/20/rainier-beachs-marjon-beauchamp-named-2019-metro-league-boys-basketball-mvp-seattle-all-metro-teams/ |publisher=Scorebook Live Washington |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=February 20, 2019}} Beauchamp guided his team to a Class 3A state semifinal appearance and fifth place in the state tournament. He averaged 26 points, 11 rebounds, and five assists per game and was named to the ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA Washington second team, [[Associated Press]] Class 3A All-State first team, and ''[[The Seattle Times]]'' All-State second team.{{cite web |title=2018-19 ALL-USA Washington Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-washington-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=April 16, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Manley |first1=Jon |title=High school basketball: 2018-19 Washington AP all-state basketball teams |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article228791744.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=April 3, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Cotterill |first1=TJ |title=Seattle Times All-State boys basketball team: All the winning sets Gonzaga Prep’s Anton Watson apart |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/seattle-times-all-state-boys-basketball-team-all-the-winning-set-gonzaga-preps-anton-watson-apart/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=March 10, 2019}} Beauchamp transferred to Dream City Christian School, a school in [[Glendale, Arizona]] with a new basketball program, for his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Obert |first1=Richard |title=5-star SF MarJon Beauchamp transferring to Dream City Christian in Arizona |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/marjon-beauchamp-transferring-to-dream-city |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=July 15, 2019}} After finishing his high school basketball career he went back to his hometown of Yakima to graduate from Eisenhower High School. ===Recruiting=== After his freshman season, Beauchamp held offers from four [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. His success on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit helped him earn a five-star rating from recruiting websites before his junior season. Beauchamp was rated a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by major recruiting services at the end of his high school career.{{cite web |title=MarJon Beauchamp |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/231073/marjon-beauchamp |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019}}{{cite web |title=MarJon Beauchamp, Dream City Christian, Small Forward |url=https://247sports.com/Player/MarJon-Beauchamp-46046880/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Marjon Beauchamp, 2020 Small forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2020/marjon-beauchamp-208339 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019}} On August 1, 2019, he announced that he would forgo [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last1=Roscher |first1=Liz |title=5-star prospect MarJon Beauchamp will skip college to prepare for 2021 NBA draft |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/5-star-prospect-mar-jon-beauchamp-will-skip-college-to-prepare-for-2021-nba-draft-163446979.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=August 1, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = MarJon Beauchamp | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Yakima, Washington|Yakima, WA]] | highschool = Dream City Christian (AZ) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 175 | 40 = | commitdate = — | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 87 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | 247 overall = 34 | rivals overall = 48 | espn overall = 44 | accessdate = April 29, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Following high school, Beauchamp trained with Chameleon BX, a training program based in [[San Francisco]], to prepare for the [[2021 NBA draft]]. After over six months with the program, he returned to Washington due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and began reconsidering his college options.{{cite web |last1=Obert |first1=Richard |title=Former Dream City star MarJon Beauchamp reassesses basketball future, looks to take college route |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/02/25/former-dream-city-star-marjon-beauchamp-looks-college-route/6824717002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=February 25, 2021}} In March 2021, Beauchamp joined the basketball team at [[Yakima Valley College]] in his hometown, being drawn by his friendship with players on the team. He tested positive for [[COVID-19]] before the season. In his college debut on April 20, 2021, Beauchamp had nine points and nine rebounds in a 99–90 loss over [[Treasure Valley Community College|Treasure Valley]], and felt lingering respiratory limitations.{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Luke |title=MarJon Beauchamp makes surprise homecoming, eager to take advantage of a short season at Yakima Valley |url=https://www.yakimaherald.com/sports/college_sports/yvcc_sports/marjon-beauchamp-makes-surprise-homecoming-eager-to-take-advantage-of-a-short-season-at-yakima/article_515c57c0-55e0-5f8c-bc47-aef6dbca3ab6.html |website=[[Yakima Herald-Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=April 24, 2021}} On June 1, he recorded a career-high 50 points and 11 rebounds in a 107–106 overtime loss to Treasure Valley.{{cite web |title=Local Report: Beauchamp drops 50 in Yakima Valley's OT basketball loss |url=https://www.yakimaherald.com/sports/college_sports/yvcc_sports/local-report-beauchamp-drops-50-in-yakima-valleys-ot-basketball-loss/article_ae6d6098-5684-5b70-9577-d3b052464c38.html |website=[[Yakima Herald-Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=June 1, 2021}} As a freshman, Beauchamp averaged 30.7 points, 10.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game through 12 games, leading the [[Northwest Athletic Conference]] in scoring.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Prospect MarJon Beauchamp signs with G League Ignite program |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32077536/prospect-marjon-beauchamp-signs-g-league-ignite |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=August 24, 2021}}{{cite web |title=Antonio Salinas, MarJon Beauchamp invited to play in The Crawsover |url=https://www.yakimaherald.com/sports/college_sports/yvcc_sports/antonio-salinas-marjon-beauchamp-invited-to-play-in-the-crawsover/article_55c7ba28-3455-5ac7-b63a-e2db1c0211a4.html |website=[[Yakima Herald-Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=July 8, 2021}} He drew attention from [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]], [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] and [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], but opted to forgo attending a Division I university due to concerns about his amateur status.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Prospect MarJon Beauchamp signs with G League Ignite program |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32077536/prospect-marjon-beauchamp-signs-g-league-ignite |access-date=August 25, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=August 25, 2021}} colspan="2"| Career | 12 || 10 || 36.4 || .525 || .398 || .768 || 10.5 || 4.8 || 1.3 || 1.1 || 30.7 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Beauchamp's father, Jon, played [[college basketball]] for [[Eastern Jon, is a former [[radio personality]] and works in customer relations in [[Bellevue, Washington]]. Beauchamp is of [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native American]] descent, from the [[Mission Indians]] and [[La Jolla Band of Luiseno Indians]].{{cite web |title=Native Prep Stars You Should Know – Washington Boys |url=https://intertribalathletics.com/2016/09/06/8-native-prep-players-you-should-know-washington/ |publisher=ITA Native Sports |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=September 6, 2016}} He is the grandson of Henry Beauchamp, the first [[African American]] mayor of Yakima.{{cite web |last1=Chen |first1=Micah |title=NBA Prospect MarJon Beauchamp Will Always Embrace Yakima Roots |url=https://1460espnyakima.com/nba-prospect-marjon-beauchamp-will-always-embrace-yakima-roots-2/ |website=[[KUTI]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=September 8, 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://goyaks.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/marjon-beauchamp/1089 Yakima Valley Yaks bio] {{NBA G League Ignite current roster}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Beauchamp, MarJon}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportspeople]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Junior college men's basketball players in the United States]] [[Category:Basketball players from Seattle]] [[Category:Native American basketball players]] [[Category:NBA G League Ignite players]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
